column1: # Jawwid Chat environment-variable manifest. Owner: AI #7 (infrastructure).
# The single machine-readable source of truth for configuration. Consumed by
# scripts/infra/check-env.sh, which CI and every deployment run.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   NAME     variable name
#   GROUP    documentation grouping
#   SECRET   yes = must come from the secret store, never from a tracked file
#   LOCAL    req | opt | forbid   -- state required in local development
#   STAGING  req | opt | forbid
#   PROD     req | opt | forbid   -- forbid = deployment is refused if present
# `forbid` is not decoration. DEBUG-style switches are forbidden in production
# so that "temporarily enable it to debug prod" is a deliberate change to this
# file and its review, not a console edit nobody sees.
#NAME
NODE_ENV
APP_ENV
TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS
PORT
# LOG_LEVEL is read by JsonLogger (apps/api/src/infra/observability/json-logger.ts)
# in BOTH processes, the API and the worker: trace | debug | info | warn | error
# | fatal. Unset or unrecognised means `info` (an unrecognised value is reported
# once at startup). Logs are JSON lines on stdout; there is no format switch.
LOG_LEVEL
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS
DATABASE_URL
DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS
# DATABASE_POOL_MAX and DATABASE_WORKER_POOL_MAX are CONSUMED by
# apps/api/src/platform/database-pool.ts: the Prisma pool of the API process and
# of the worker process, added to DATABASE_URL as connection_limit. The 1 GiB
# managed database has 22 usable connections; at 7 + 3, a deploy that briefly
# runs old and new side by side uses 20. Unset locally means Prisma's default.
DATABASE_POOL_MAX
DATABASE_WORKER_POOL_MAX
REDIS_URL
QUEUE_PREFIX
WORKER_CONCURRENCY
JWT_ACCESS_SECRET
JWT_REFRESH_SECRET
JWT_ACCESS_TTL
JWT_REFRESH_TTL
# RESET_CODE_HASH_SECRET is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/platform/auth/password-reset.service.ts
# (PD-43): the HMAC key under which every one-time code -- a reset (PD-21/PD-25)
# or a first sign-in code -- is stored, so a database read or a backup cannot
# recover a live code. At least 32 characters. Required in staging and
# production: without it no code is issued or accepted (fails closed). Locally
# a key is derived from JWT_REFRESH_SECRET. Rotating it voids every live code.
# Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 48
RESET_CODE_HASH_SECRET
# STORAGE. Two kinds of row live here, and the difference matters when reading
# this file against the code.
# Read by the implementation that exists today: STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET (the API
# refuses to start without it), STORAGE_ENDPOINT, STORAGE_SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS,
# STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT and the ATTACHMENT_MAX_* ceilings.
# Reserved for the S3-compatible backend the seam is built for: STORAGE_REGION,
# STORAGE_BUCKET, STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY, STORAGE_SECRET_KEY. No code reads these
# yet -- OBJECT_STORAGE is bound to the reference SignedLocalObjectStorage and no
# adapter exists (findings.md RT-022). They stay declared because this file
# states the deployment contract rather than the current call graph, exactly as
# the FCM_*/APNS_* rows do while PUSH_PROVIDER is still LoggingPushProvider, and
# because docker-compose.yml already provisions the local S3-compatible service
# they configure. Deleting them would take the local stack and inventory.md with
# them. No provider has been chosen; nothing here chooses one.
STORAGE_ENDPOINT
STORAGE_REGION
STORAGE_BUCKET
STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY
STORAGE_SECRET_KEY
STORAGE_SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS
# How long the S3 client waits (s3-object-storage.ts, STORAGE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS).
# Optional everywhere: unset means 3000 ms to connect and 5000 ms to response
# headers per attempt, 3 attempts (the SDK's own count, so 503 SlowDown keeps its
# retries). A hung endpoint then costs a call -- or a media read, whose HEAD + GET
# share one budget -- about 15 s instead of minutes. CopyObject has its own 60 s
# per attempt. NOT a limit on a streamed body: a slow reader may pause a video
# for as long as it likes. Out-of-range values refuse to start (connect
STORAGE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS
STORAGE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
STORAGE_MAX_ATTEMPTS
STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET
# RT-037 (2026-10-14): attachment and story media links point at THIS API's
# access-checked media route. The base is MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL when set (the
# public origin + /api/v1, e.g. behind a CDN or a path-rewriting proxy), else the
# origin each request reached the API at. Optional everywhere.
MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
# Where the local reference blob store keeps bytes. Optional everywhere because
# the code defaults it (blob-store.ts) -- but the default is the OS temp
# directory, which no deployment should rely on: it is per-instance and does not
# survive a restart. Setting this names a path; it does not make that path
# durable or shared. Durability is a hosting decision, not a manifest one.
STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT
# The public base URL of this API's own /storage route, used ONLY by the local
# reference storage to mint signed URLs a client can reach. Optional everywhere
# because the code defaults it to localhost -- which is correct on a laptop and
# wrong on anything a client reaches over a network, so any such deployment that
# runs the local implementation must set it. It is NOT an alternative spelling of
# STORAGE_ENDPOINT: that variable is the S3 service endpoint, and its presence is
# what selects the S3 backend. Neither falls back to the other.
STORAGE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
OUTBOX_POLL_MS
OUTBOX_BATCH_SIZE
OUTBOX_IDLE_BACKOFF_MS
# How many realtime deliveries one API node runs at once (delivery-queue.ts):
# each holds a pool connection, so unset means a third of DATABASE_POOL_MAX
# (at least 1; 2 when that is unset too). Order within a conversation holds at
# any value. 1..16; anything else refuses to start.
REALTIME_DELIVERY_CONCURRENCY
ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES_IMAGE
ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES_VIDEO
ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES_VOICE
ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES_FILE
# Ceiling on the duration a sender may claim for a voice note. The server never
# decodes the audio, so this bounds an assertion rather than a measurement.
ATTACHMENT_MAX_VOICE_DURATION_MS
# PD-29 Materials (apps/api/src/materials/materials-config.ts). The academy's
# lessons site (a lesson item stores its PATH only, joined to this base when
# opened, so the site can move to a pinned snapshot origin without a
# migration), and the https origins a link may be framed from (the site's
# origin is always included; any other link opens in the browser). Unset: the
# lessons are not offered. Optional everywhere; Admin Web's frame-src reads its
# own MATERIALS_FRAME_ORIGINS.
MATERIALS_SITE_BASE_URL
MATERIALS_FRAME_ORIGINS
# LESSON_APPROVALS_SIGNING_KEY is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/lesson-content/approvals-signer.ts
# (PD-49): the Ed25519 private key that signs the export of children's Quran
# content approvals. Its PUBLIC key is committed with its id in
# apps/lessons/src/content/approvals-keys.json, and CI refuses any approvals file
# it does not verify. Optional: unset, the API exports nothing (503) and no
# content reaches a child. An owner action (docs/infrastructure/secrets.md).
# PEM PKCS#8, or its base64 DER. Generate with: openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519
LESSON_APPROVALS_SIGNING_KEY
FCM_PROJECT_ID
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
APNS_KEY_ID
APNS_TEAM_ID
APNS_BUNDLE_ID
APNS_PRIVATE_KEY
APNS_PRODUCTION
# Calling is LiveKit Cloud; there is no local LiveKit server in docker-compose, so
# a developer machine and a unit/integration test run leave it unconfigured. The
# issuer refuses to mint a token when any of the three is absent (media-token.ts),
# so an unconfigured local environment cannot call and cannot pretend to -- which is
# why these are opt locally and req everywhere a client actually connects. Same
# shape, and same reason, as the push group above.
# The token TTL is deliberately NOT here: it lives in chat.config as
# `call.token_ttl_seconds`, which is what CallService reads when it mints a media
# token. An env var would be a knob that changes nothing.
LIVEKIT_URL
LIVEKIT_API_KEY
LIVEKIT_API_SECRET
CORE_BASE_URL
CORE_API_KEY
CORE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
CORE_TIMEOUT_MS
CORE_RETRY_MAX
# BACKUP. Read by scripts/infra/backup-db.sh and restore-db.sh -- the BACKUP
# JOB's environment, not the API's. A backup is a complete copy of every
# family's messages, so backup-db.sh REFUSES to write an unencrypted one unless
# APP_ENV is local, test or ci, and it decides that before pg_dump runs. That
# enforcement lives in the script because the script is what would write the
# file; check-env.sh validates the API process, which never reads these, so they
# are `opt` here rather than `req`.
# Set exactly one. The key file (a path; its first line is the secret; mode 600)
# is preferred: a path is not a secret, and a file is not inherited by every
# child process the way an environment variable is. Format and recovery-by-hand:
# docs/infrastructure/backup-recovery.md §3.
BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE
BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE
# TEACHER_PAYOUT_KEYS is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/teacher-file (PD-18): the keys
# that seal a teacher's payout account details (AES-256-GCM) before they reach
# the database. `keyid:base64key[,keyid:base64key...]`, each key 32 bytes; the
# first seals, every listed key opens (rotation). Unset = payout accounts can be
# neither saved nor revealed (503) -- payroll fails closed, never in clear. Losing
# the key loses every saved account: back it up with the database backups' key.
# Generate one with: echo "k1:$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
TEACHER_PAYOUT_KEYS
# STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/billing (PD-27): card payments
# through Stripe Checkout (the payment link's "Pay by card", the app's Pay) and
# card refunds. Unset = no card option is offered anywhere and a checkout
# answers 503; bank transfers and cash work without it. Restricted key scopes:
# Checkout Sessions write, Refunds write.
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
# STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is CONSUMED by POST /api/v1/stripe/webhook (PD-27): the
# endpoint's signing secret (whsec_...). A card payment is recorded ONLY from a
# webhook this secret verifies. Unset = the webhook answers 503 and Stripe
# retries for three days.
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
# PAYMENT_LINK_BASE_URL is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/billing (PD-27): the public
# origin plus /api/v1 that payment links are built on, e.g.
# https://api.jawwid.com/api/v1. Unset = the origin of the request that made
# the link (fine locally; set it wherever a proxy rewrites the host).
PAYMENT_LINK_BASE_URL
# SUBSCRIPTION_LOCK_ENFORCED is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/platform/subscription-lock.ts
# (PD-30) in the API and the worker: 'true' enforces the payment lock -- a locked
# child's group is read-only for the parent and teacher, calls and bookings are
# refused, lessons are put on hold and the cards go out. Anything else (or
# unset) = off: the ledger, the balance and the state are still computed and
# shown, and nothing is refused. Owner decision 2026-10-26: on in staging, off in
# production until the owner turns it on (the deploy workflows default it so).
SUBSCRIPTION_LOCK_ENFORCED
# TEACHER_SUPERVISOR_STRICT_SCOPE is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/platform/teacher-scope.ts
# (PD-35) in the API and the worker, which write it into chat.config at boot so
# the database's scope decision reads the same value: 'true' = a teacher
# supervisor works on the teachers assigned to them only (the Teachers Manager
# and the super admin on every teacher); '1', 'yes' and 'on' (any case) count
# as 'true' too. Any other value = off: the Teachers
# department works department-wide, as before PD-35, while teachers are being
# assigned. UNSET writes nothing: the stored value stands (off until written);
# a boot that changes it logs a warning. Runbook: docs/admin/pd035-teacher-supervisors.md. Department head decision 2026-10-26: off everywhere until the
# owner turns it on (the deploy workflows default it so).
TEACHER_SUPERVISOR_STRICT_SCOPE
# SALES_FAMILY_SCOPE is CONSUMED by apps/api/src/platform/sales-scope.ts (PD-42)
# in the API, which writes it into chat.config at boot so the database's write
# guards read the same value: 'own' = a Sales member reads and writes only the
# families they own (the Sales manager keeps every family); 'all' = every
# Sales member reads every family, as before PD-42. Any other value REFUSES TO
# BOOT (fail closed). UNSET writes nothing: the stored value stands ('all'
# until written); a boot that changes it logs a warning. The deploy workflows
# do NOT default it. Owner decision 2026-10-28: 'own' only after the intake
# from Jawwid Core is complete and verified.
SALES_FAMILY_SCOPE
# SENTRY_DSN is CONSUMED: when set, the API and the worker report 5xx responses,
# swallowed worker-subsystem failures and process-level faults to Sentry
# (apps/api/src/infra/observability/sentry-error-tracker.ts); when unset or
# empty, error tracking is inert and @sentry/node is never loaded. Every event
# is rebuilt from an allowlist before it leaves (no request, body, user,
# breadcrumbs or stack-frame variables) -- docs/infrastructure/monitoring.md 3a.
# The Sentry environment is APP_ENV and the release is GIT_COMMIT, so there is
# no SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT or SENTRY_RELEASE: one source of truth per fact.
SENTRY_DSN
# OTEL_* are `opt` EVERYWHERE, and that is a correction rather than a relaxation.
# They were `req` in production while NO CODE READS THEM -- there is no
# OpenTelemetry SDK in apps/api/package.json and no `OTEL_` reference in src/.
# A release was therefore refused unless an operator supplied an endpoint that
# nothing would ever export to, which teaches people that this file's
# requirements are decorative -- the opposite of what `forbid` below is for.
# Flip them back to `req` in the same commit that wires an OTLP exporter.
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG
HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS
GIT_COMMIT
BUILD_VERSION
BUILD_TIME
# PD-25 parent self-recovery (apps/api/src/account-recovery/recovery-delivery.ts).
# Each channel is OFF until all of its variables are set, and the sign-in screen
# hides a channel that is off (GET /auth/recovery/options): e-mail needs
# SMTP_URL + RECOVERY_MAIL_FROM; WhatsApp needs WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID +
# WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN + WHATSAPP_RECOVERY_TEMPLATE (an APPROVED Meta
# authentication template). SMTP_URL embeds the SMTP password, so it is secret.
# REQUIRED in production (department head, 2026-10-28): e-mail also carries the
# first-login and reset codes staff and teachers depend on (PD-40, PD-43), so a
# production without it strands people at sign-in. Both halves are required:
# SMTP_URL alone still leaves the e-mail channel off.
SMTP_URL
RECOVERY_MAIL_FROM
WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN
WHATSAPP_RECOVERY_TEMPLATE
WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE
WHATSAPP_API_VERSION
PRISMA_MIGRATE_SKIP_GENERATE
DEBUG
PRISMA_STUDIO
USE_MOCK_PUSH
USE_MOCK_CORE
ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS
# PD-25: writes recovery codes to the API log instead of sending them. The API
# also refuses to boot with it under NODE_ENV=production.
RECOVERY_DELIVERY_LOG
